text: Sixteen lessons ago, this started as two stakeholders wanting more than a one-time pull. Here's what that turned into: a real five-table T-SQL join, staged into a reusable fact view and two dimension views, altered in place later without breaking anything downstream.

A real star schema, with actual relationships and a proper Date table, not a single flat result. DAX measures built with CALCULATE, DATEADD, ALL, AVERAGEX, and DIVIDE, a real step up from plain SUM and DISTINCTCOUNT. Two report pages, each designed around how its specific stakeholder actually works, plus a real scheduled refresh through the On-premises Data Gateway.

It would have been easy to design this project without a bug in it. That's not what real BI work looks like. Reproduce, isolate the variable, confirm with a controlled test, fix without touching correct code, document it, and communicate it two different ways. The numbers don't match is one of the most common tickets any BI developer gets, and diagnosing it calmly is the actual skill.

The Beginner project was one stakeholder, one page, built once. This project added real breadth: multiple tables, two pages, a schedule, a bug, a change request. Each one is a genuine step up in scope and responsibility, not just more content.

The path's Advanced capstone goes further still, with larger, more production-style builds. Everything you just did, staging, modeling, CALCULATE-based DAX, real diagnosis, communicating across audiences, is exactly the foundation that next tier builds on. You're not starting over. You're building up.
